cost_of_revenue.calculation_note: Cost of revenue — Condensed Consolidated Statements of Income, Page 5

operating_expenses.calculation_note: Sum of Research and development (17,699) + Marketing and sales (2,908) + General and administrative (2,614) = 23,221 — Condensed Consolidated Statements of Income, Page 5. Cost of revenue excluded.

cash_and_equivalents.calculation_note: Cash and cash equivalents — Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets, Page 6

short_term_debt.calculation_note: No short-term debt or current portion of long-term debt line item identified on the Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets (Page 6). Current liabilities consist of Accounts payable, Operating lease liabilities (current), and Accrued expenses and other current liabilities — none represent borrowed capital.

long_term_debt.calculation_note: Long-term debt — Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets, Page 6

net_debt.calculation_note: Short-term debt (0) + Long-term debt (58,748) - Cash & Cash Equivalents (23,426) = Net debt (35,322) — Balance Sheet, Page 6

capital_expenditure.calculation_note: Purchases of property and equipment — Condensed Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, Page 7

free_cash_flow.calculation_note: Free cash flow — Reconciliation of GAAP to Non-GAAP Results, Page 9. Calculated as Net cash provided by operating activities (32,226) minus Purchases of property and equipment (18,997) minus Principal payments on finance leases (843).

shares_outstanding.calculation_note: Total shares outstanding at period end date not explicitly disclosed in the financial statements provided.

shares_weighted_average_diluted.calculation_note: Weighted-average shares used to compute earnings per share — Diluted — Condensed Consolidated Statements of Income, Page 5

narrative.summary: Total revenue grew 33% year-over-year to $56.31 billion, driven by a 19% increase in ad impressions and a 12% rise in average price per ad. On a constant currency basis, revenue growth was 29%, reflecting a foreign exchange tailwind of approximately 4 percentage points.

Total costs and expenses rose 35% year-over-year to $33.44 billion, with R&D as the largest component at $17.70 billion. Operating margin held steady at 41%, matching Q1 2025 despite the elevated cost growth.

Net income increased 61% year-over-year to $26.77 billion, significantly boosted by an $8.03 billion income tax benefit from U.S. Treasury Notice 2026-7 related to the Corporate Alternative Minimum Tax treatment of previously capitalized R&D costs. Excluding this benefit, diluted EPS would have been $3.13 lower.

Family of Apps revenue grew to $55.91 billion with operating income of $26.90 billion, while Reality Labs revenue declined slightly to $402 million with an operating loss of $4.03 billion. FoA remains the dominant profit driver, with RL continuing to invest heavily in VR/AR development.

narrative.topic: Capital Expenditure and Free Cash Flow
narrative.summary: Capital expenditures (including finance lease principal payments) were $19.84 billion in Q1 2026, reflecting heavy infrastructure investment. Free cash flow was $12.39 billion, up from $10.33 billion in Q1 2025, supported by strong operating cash flow of $32.23 billion.

Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $81.18 billion as of March 31, 2026. Total assets grew to $395.25 billion, with property and equipment net of $194.78 billion reflecting ongoing infrastructure build-out.

Family daily active people averaged 3.56 billion in March 2026, up 4% year-over-year, though a slight quarter-over-quarter decline was attributed to internet disruptions in Iran and WhatsApp access restrictions in Russia.

Q2 2026 revenue is guided to $58–61 billion with a ~2% foreign currency tailwind. Full-year 2026 expenses are expected at $162–169 billion, while capital expenditures guidance was raised to $125–145 billion (from $115–135 billion) due to higher component pricing and additional data center costs.

Meta flagged ongoing legal and regulatory risks in the EU and U.S., including youth-related issues with additional trials scheduled in 2026 that may result in material losses. Macroeconomic, geopolitical, and competitive risks are also cited as potential headwinds.
